statements.statement: M has only monic arrows and identity endomorphisms; N denotes object isomorphism classes ordered by existence of arrows, and J_n the subobjects of D_n.
statements.type: carried as background without fault found

statements.place: Upper type application, image and greatest-element fiber
statements.statement: The domain-isomorphism-class map tau_n on J_n is strictly increasing, has image N_{<=n}, and tau_n inverse(n)={d_n}.
statements.argument: If subobjects x=[a:X->D_n] and y=[b:Y->D_n] satisfy x<=y, write a=b h; then [X]<=[Y]. If [X]=[Y], choose an isomorphism s:Y->X. Both s h and h s are endomorphisms, hence identities, so h is an isomorphism and x=y. Thus x<y forces strict inequality of types. Every type in the image is <=n because its representative maps to D_n; conversely an arrow from a representative of any n-prime<=n is monic and supplies that type. All x lie below d_n and tau_n(d_n)=n; strict increase therefore forces a subobject of type n to equal d_n.
statements.outcome: Passed under the recorded hypotheses and reachability order. Strict increase does not assert injectivity on incomparable subobjects.

statements.place: First two-row Hom map and bijection onto tau_n inverse(n-prime)
statements.statement: Arrows D_n-prime -> D_n correspond bijectively to subobjects of D_n having type n-prime.
statements.argument: An arrow is monic and hence represents such a subobject. Equality of the subobjects represented by u and v gives an automorphism a of D_n-prime with u=v a; the endomorphism hypothesis gives a=id. Conversely a representative m:X->D_n of type n-prime can be composed with an isomorphism D_n-prime->X, yielding an arrow representing the same subobject. The notation u(d_n-prime) is interpreted as the image of the top subobject under the induced subobject map u_*, so it equals [u].
statements.outcome: Passed. The displayed use of u on a subobject is an induced-action convention, not an editorial glyph correction.

statements.place: Lower induced-map construction and commutative evaluation diagram
statements.statement: The map rho from the type-n-prime fiber to Hom(J_n-prime,J_n) is injective, and evaluation at d_n-prime composes with rho to the inclusion into J_n.
statements.argument: Use the unique arrow u representing a fiber element xi. Composition defines u_*([a:A->D_n-prime])=[u a], independent of the domain-equivalence representative. Factorizations are preserved; if [u a]<=[u b], an equation u a=u b h cancels by monicity of u to a=b h, so order is also reflected. Evaluating u_* at the top identity subobject gives [u]=xi. Thus evaluation composed with rho is the fiber inclusion and rho is injective.
statements.outcome: Passed for the fiber with type n-prime and ambient n. This does not decide the ink order of the two indices at any occurrence.

statements.place: Definition J_{n-prime,n} versus final diagram first object, confirmed in main26 and main34
statements.statement: With the displayed definition J_{a,b}=tau_b inverse(a), the rho_{n,n-prime} construction has domain J_{n-prime,n}; reversing that displayed pair gives a different type in general.
statements.argument: The preceding construction fixes the target object D_n and the type n-prime of its subobject. By the displayed definition the fiber is J_{n-prime,n}. The pair J_{n,n-prime} would instead denote type n inside J_n-prime and cannot be substituted without an additional equality of the two indices.
statements.outcome: Type discrepancy confirmed against the ink: definition J_{n-prime,n}, final-diagram first object J_{n,n-prime}. Both manuscript orders are preserved; the mathematical expectation is recorded only here.
